bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Patna protests intensify as Prashant Kishor backs students, farmers | MorungExpress
bihar_raw_news.content: (Photo: IANS) India 25th August 2026 Patna, August 25 (IANS) Patna witnessed a tense day on Tuesday as student organisations protesting recruitment and examination issues joined farmers opposing the proposed Pataliputra Greenfield Satellite Township in demonstrations across the city. Police erected barricades at several locations to prevent student protesters from marching towards Lok Bhavan. Reacting to the police action, Bankipur MLA Prashant Kishor said recent events had demonstrated the strength of democracy. He argued that authorities now appeared to think twice before using force against protesters, describing this as a positive development. Kishor urged the government to address what he termed the legitimate demands of students and farmers, saying such concerns could not simply be suppressed. He highlighted issues including alleged privatisation and commercialisation of education, the growing influence of coaching institutes, examination paper leaks, rising unemployment and dissatisfaction among youth. He warned that failing to address these concerns could lead to larger student movements in the future. When reporters told him student aspirants were looking for him, Kishor said he was already in Patna and regularly moving around the city. Alongside the student protests, farmers from Punpun, Naubatpur, Masaurhi, Fatuha and surrounding areas demonstrated against the township project. Kishor backed their concerns, alleging that the government’s land policy could benefit major industrialists at farmers' expense. He claimed valuable agricultural land could be transferred at inadequate prices, arguing that the policy was difficult to implement in Bihar and warning that attempts to acquire large areas of productive land could lead to widespread unrest. Farmers said their agricultural land was their primary source of livelihood and that they produced three crops a year. They argued that surrendering land would threaten their families’ ability to fund education, marriages and other essential expenses. Protesters demanded the government reconsider the proposed acquisition, maintaining they did not want to surrender their land. Patna District Magistrate, SSP and SP reached the protest site and held discussions with farmer representatives, attempting to persuade them to resolve the matter through dialogue. The Bihar government has proposed developing 12 townships across the state, including the Pataliputra Greenfield Satellite Township. Farmers opposing the Patna project insist their agricultural land should not be acquired for development.

bihar_raw_news.title: Nationwide caste census: Congress seeks Telangana, Bihar models to ensure accurate BC ...
bihar_raw_news.content: TOP STORIES HYDERABAD CRIME NATION FACT CHECK Fact Check English Fact Check Telugu Fact Check Tamil Fact Check Kannada Fact Check Malayalam Fact Check Health Now You Know AI/Deepfake What's Next Consumer Voice DATA STORIES SATELLITE JOURNALISM LIFESTYLE HEALTH EDUCATION/JOBS Business / Tech & Startups REGIONAL Andhra Pradesh HYDERABAD SOUTH INDIA TELANGANA Tirupati VISAKHAPATNAM Vijayawada/Amaravati WARANGAL World / NRI News Nationwide caste census: Congress seeks Telangana, Bihar models to ensure accurate BC, OBC data The present methodology used by the Central Government is not considering the Backward Classes (BCs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in society, the party leaders said. By Newsmeter Network Published on : 25 Aug 2026 7:01 PM IST New Delhi: Adopting the methodology of the Telangana and Bihar models for the upcoming nationwide caste census is essential for ensuring accurate data and true social justice, the Indian National Congress said. The present methodology used by the Central Government is not considering the Backward Classes (BCs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in society, the party leaders said. ‘Make separate record in census for BCs and OBCs’ G Niranjan, chairman of Telangana State Backward Classes Commission, has written a letter to the Registrar General of India, Census Commissioner and the Home Minister Amit Shah demanding that the status of BCs and OBCs must be separately recorded by the census. The letters from the chairman and delegations of the Congress party in Telangana have asked the Congress leadership to demand that there must be separate columns for recording other castes. Scrap current notification Demanding that the Centre scrap the current notification and replicate the Telangana and Bihar frameworks at the national level, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging an immediate course correction Importance of Bihar and Telangana caste surveys Congress General Secretary In Charge of Communications Jairam Ramesh highlighted that the detailed models executed in Telangana and Bihar provide the only reliable roadmap for an authentic exercise. He noted that both states successfully prepared standardised, state-specific lists of castes and utilised structured questionnaires to ensure precision. Ramesh asserted that without adopting these proven methodologies, an accurate assessment of the population and socio-economic status of various communities, particularly OBCs, will remain impossible. Highlights of the statement from Congress leaders - Mandate the Drop-Down System: The Congress leaders insisted that the census questionnaire must replace open-ended responses with a standardised ‘drop-down’ menu format based on existing State and Central caste lists. Ramesh warned that open-ended questions lead to extreme data distortion and duplication, whereas the Telangana model ensures seamless categorisation for enumerators. - Rejection of Union Home Ministry Format: The party explicitly rejected the Union Home Ministry’s August 14 notification containing 40 questions, where caste is relegated to a single open-ended query at serial number 10. The party termed this format ‘deception,’ ‘betrayal,’ and a deliberate ‘whitewash’ aimed at sabotaging meaningful social justice policies. - Third Unanswered Representation: The August 20 joint letter by Kharge

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar participates in national conference of Information and Public Relations Secretaries
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar participates in national conference of Information and Public Relations Secretaries ANI | Updated: Aug 25, 2026 19:42 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], August 25 (ANI): Bihar Information and Public Relations Department Secretary Naveen Kumar represented the State at the national conference of Information and Public Relations Secretaries from States and Union Territories held at Vigyan Bhawan in the national capital on Tuesday. Senior officials from the Central Government, including the Secretary of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Chanchal Kumar, along with representatives from various States and Union Territories, attended the conference. The conference aimed to make information and public communication systems between the Centre and States more effective, adopt new mechanisms in line with the evolving media landscape and strengthen mutual coordination. Discussions were held on various policy and operational matters concerning the information and broadcasting sector, according to the release. A key focus of the conference was strengthening the partnership between the Press Information Bureau (PIB) and Information and Public Relations Departments of States and Union Territories. The meeting also discussed utilisation of training facilities at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC) for capacity building of Information and Public Relations officers. The conference also covered the framework for WAVES 2027, enhancing market access through 'WAVES Bazaar', expanding public service broadcasting infrastructure and making state-specific programmes and public outreach more effective. Deliberations also included adoption of the 'India Cine Hub' single-window portal for film shooting and live event permissions, as well as increasing state participation in public service broadcasting. The agenda further included the transition to a digital system through the 'Press Sewa Portal' under the Press and Registration of Periodicals (PRP) Act, 2023, promoting low-cost cinema in rural and underserved areas, implementing accessibility standards in cinema halls and making the 'WaveX State Ecosystem' effective. Bihar 's participation in the conference was aimed at aligning the State's information and public relations system with emerging technologies, digital media and institutional frameworks at the national level, according to the release. The conference provided a platform for the exchange of experiences and best practices, as well as for strengthening coordination and capacity building between the Centre and the states. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Plans ₹70000-Crore Ganga Marine Drive - eGov Magazine - Elets Technomedia
bihar_raw_news.content: Home · News Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has announced a plan to develop a 126-kilometre Marine Drive along the Ganga , with an estimated investment of ₹70,000 crore . The proposed corridor would extend the state’s riverfront road network from the Patna region towards Koilwar on the Son River. The announcement was made on August 23 during the concluding ceremony of an Employment Fair at Gyan Bhawan near Gandhi Maidan in Patna. The Chief Minister said the project is aimed at improving infrastructure while creating employment and attracting private investment. Advertisement ₹70,000 Crore Investment Proposed According to the plan outlined by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the proposed investment would be divided between the state government and the private sector. The proposed structure is: ₹20,000 crore – Bihar government contribution ₹50,000 crore – Expected private-sector investment ₹70,000 crore – Total estimated investment 126 km – Proposed length of the corridor Choudhary said the project would create new opportunities for investment and employment along the proposed route. J.P. Ganga Path to Form the Base The proposed corridor will build on the existing J.P. Ganga Path in Patna, which has become popularly known as the city’s Marine Drive. According to the Chief Minister, the existing road stretch is around 21 kilometres long . The project was initiated in 2013 and completed in 2025 at an estimated cost of around ₹6,000 crore. The new proposal would significantly expand the riverfront road network beyond Patna and connect it with a much longer stretch along the Ganga. Corridor to Connect Infrastructure and Economic Growth The government is presenting the proposed Marine Drive as more than a connectivity project. The extended corridor is expected to create opportunities for economic activity and private-sector participation. The project could support: Improved river-side road connectivity Expansion of infrastructure along the Ganga Greater private investment New employment opportunities Growth of commercial and economic activities Wider urban and regional connectivity Announcement Made at Employment Fair The project announcement came during an employment-focused programme organised by the Department of Youth, Employment and Skill Development . Offer letters were distributed to candidates selected by various employers during the event. The government linked the proposed infrastructure investment with its wider focus on employment generation and creating new economic opportunities for young people. Government and Private Sector to Share Investment The proposed financing model places a significant share of the investment on the private sector, with ₹50,000 crore expected to come from private entities. The Bihar government has proposed contributing ₹20,000 crore towards the project. The detailed financing structure, implementation mechanism and execution plan will determine how the proposal moves forward. Proposed Corridor Could Expand Bihar’s Riverfront Network If implemented, the 126-km Marine Drive would represent a major expansion of Bihar’s existing riverfront infrastructure. The proposal would take the concept of the J.P. Ganga Path beyond Patna and create a much larger corridor along the Ganga, potentially supporting connectivity, investment and employment across the region. For now, the ₹70,000-crore, 126-km Marine Drive remains a government proposal

bihar_raw_news.title: Kharge, Rahul Gandhi urge PM Modi to scrap caste census questionnaire
bihar_raw_news.content: Kharge, Rahul Gandhi urge PM Modi to scrap caste census questionnaire Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi have urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to scrap the existing caste census questionnaire and formulate a new one after consulting political parties, experts and the public, citing Telangana and Bihar's caste surveys as examples. By PTI Published Date - 25 August 2026, 05:32 PM New Delhi: Leaders of Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the caste census issue, demanding that the government scrap the existing questionnaire for it and formulate a new one after consulting political parties, experts, and the general public. Kharge and Gandhi said they do not accept the caste census being conducted in the current manner and urged the government to take a cue from the caste surveys done in Telangana and Bihar. Briefing reporters on the letter written in Hindi by Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Kharge and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Gandhi on August 20, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the government’s current efforts towards a caste census are just a “whitewash”. Ramesh noted that this is the third letter written by the Congress leadership to Modi over the issue but has not received any reply. In their letter, Kharge and Gandhi said social justice policies in India cannot be effectively implemented without accurate data and a precise assessment of the numerical strength and socio-economic status of various castes is possible only if the caste enumeration is conducted correctly. “Your government has opted for an open-ended question format to record caste details in the census, which is misleading. Under this method, whatever name an individual provides for their caste will be recorded as it is,” the leaders said in their letter to Modi. In India, the same caste is known by different names, sub-castes, and linguistic variations across different regions, Congress president Kharge and former party chief Rahul Gandhi pointed out. Consequently, if members of the same caste are recorded under different names during the census, a single caste could end up being fragmented into thousands of distinct names, they argued. This would result in a list of hundreds of thousands of caste names, rendering the entire dataset obtained from the caste census useless, Kharge and Gandhi argued. “If the actual population of a community is not accurately recorded, any assessment of its status will also be flawed. This will disadvantage backward, extremely backward, and other marginalised communities, and will impact decisions related to education, employment, welfare schemes, and social justice,” Kharge and Gandhi said. Most importantly, this approach will fail to reveal the size of the OBC population in India, as the term “Backward Class” is not even included in this census, they said. “An easy solution for this already exists: a drop-down list of castes should be created. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Raises Concerns Over Renewal of Farakka Water Treaty - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Rapid Fire Prev Next Bihar Raises Concerns Over Renewal of Farakka Water Treaty 25 Aug 2026 3 min read Tags: Rapid Fire CA Quick Facts For Prelims GS Paper - 2 GS Paper - 3 Source: IE The possible renewal of the 1996 India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Sharing Treaty (Farakka Treaty) , set to expire in December 2026, has triggered a debate in Bihar, with the state seeking safeguards for concerns related to flooding, siltation, and dry-season water availability. Ganga Water Sharing Treaty (Farakka Treaty): The India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Sharing Treaty was signed on 12th December 1996 between India and Bangladesh to regulate the sharing of Ganga waters at the Farakka Barrage during the dry season (1st January to 31st May). The treaty established a 30-year framework (1996–2026) for predictable water sharing and replaced earlier short-term arrangements such as the 1977 Ganga Water Agreement. It provides a formula-based mechanism for sharing Ganga waters during the lean season. Unlike the 1977 agreement, the 1996 treaty does not contain a guaranteed minimum flow clause. If the available flow falls below 50,000 cusecs, both countries are required to enter into emergency consultations. Farakka Barrage: The Farakka Barrage , located on the Ganga River in Murshidabad district, West Bengal , was constructed and operationalised in 1975. The barrage was built to divert water from the Ganga through a feeder canal into the Hooghly River to reduce silt accumulation and maintain the navigability of the Kolkata Port . Bangladesh’s Concerns: Reduced downstream flow affects water availability, soil salinity, agriculture, and ecosystems in southern Bangladesh. Bihar’s Concerns: Farakka Barrage has contributed to a “flood-and-parch” situation , with concerns over increased silt deposition, rising riverbed levels, reduced river carrying capacity, frequent monsoon flooding in districts such as Bhagalpur and Munger , and reduced dry-season water availability. Bihar has sought consideration of its projected water requirements up to 2050 , along with scientific silt management strategies and greater representation of affected states , in any future revision of the Ganga Water Sharing Treaty. Joint Rivers Commission (JRC): India and Bangladesh address shared river management issues through the Joint Rivers Commission (JRC) , established in 1972 to promote cooperation over common water resources. The commission facilitates exchange of hydrological data, discussions on transboundary river issues, and cooperation in the development and management of shared water resources . Ganga Basin Challenges: The Ganga basin faces complex river management challenges, including sedimentation, changing river dynamics due to climate variability, groundwater alterations, upstream water withdrawals, and the need for integrated basin-level management . bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar SIR Judgment Clarifies That Electoral Roll Exclusion Won't Result In Loss Of Other Rights
bihar_raw_news.content: Login Account Subscribe Premium Home / Top Stories / Bihar SIR Judgment Clarifies That... Bihar SIR Judgment Clarifies That Electoral Roll Exclusion Won't Result In Loss Of Other Rights : Supreme Court Debby Jain 25 Aug 2026 4:19 PM IST Share this Listen to this Article The Supreme Court on Tuesday orally said that its judgment in the Bihar SIR matter has held that the deletion from the electoral roll per se will not lead to the loss of other citizenship benefits. During the hearing of the West Bengal SIR matter today, the Court was told that persons excluded from electoral rolls are being deprived of ration under the Public Distribution System scheme, and other benefits, such as domicile certificates. Senior Advocate Rauf Rahim , for petitioners, urged a bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana to pass an order that there should not be such a "ripple effect" following exclusion from electoral rolls due to SIR. The bench however did not record pass any such order. CJI Surya Kant said that the Court was now only focusing on issues relating to the pending appeals in the tribunals, and other issues can be raised before the High Court. When Rauf submitted that one word from the Supreme Court can prevent such "ripple effects" of SIR exclusions, Justice Bagchi said that in the Bihar SIR judgment , the Court had clarified the effect of electoral roll exclusion over a person's entitlement under social welfare schemes. "We have already clarified our position. In the Bihar SIR judgment, we had made clear that what is the [...] and the exclusion from the voters list qua rights of an individual in social security schemes", Justice Bagchi said. Notably, in the Bihar SIR judgment, the Court had held that ECI cannot decide citizenship of a person and the conclusions reached by it (after SIR) would be relevant only for electoral purposes. "The Commission is empowered, in the exercise of its constitutional mandate, to undertake a limited enquiry into citizenship for the purpose of satisfying itself as to eligibility for inclusion in the electoral roll. Such an enquiry does not amount to a determination of citizenship in the strict sense, and any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone. The consequence of such a determination is correspondingly limited. It affects the individual's entitlement to be included in the electoral roll, and thereby their right to participate in the electoral process. It does not, however, operate to divest the individual of claims of citizenship, nor does it foreclose a determination of that question by the Competent Authority under the Citizenship Act " the Court had said. The bench observed that persons aggrieved by denial of any social welfare benefits after electoral roll-exclusion have the option to approach the High Court. bihar_raw_news.title: India's mushroom production surges, led by Bihar , but challenges remain | Agriculture
bihar_raw_news.content: Home / Industry / Agriculture / India's mushroom production surges, led by Bihar, but challenges remain India's mushroom production surges, led by Bihar, but challenges remain India's mushroom output rose from 51,000 tonnes in 2015 to 347,750 tonnes in 2024, with Bihar at the forefront, but productivity, cold-chain and infrastructure gaps threaten further growth. premium Mushroom Sanjeeb Mukherjee New Delhi 7 min read Last Updated : Aug 25 2026 | 6:46 PM IST Listen to This Article If one were to prepare a list of crops whose production has shown exponential growth over the past decade or so, mushrooms would figure prominently in such a ranking. India’s mushroom production has jumped exponentially in the nine years from 2015 to 2024, rising from a mere 51,000 tonnes to almost 347,750 tonnes and registering a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 23.76 per cent, according to country-wise records maintained by the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). In comparison, China, which remained the world’s largest producer of mushrooms of all kinds for both edible and non-edible purposes and accounted for almost 94 per cent of annual global output, registered a production CAGR of just 3.80 per cent between 2015 and 2024. During the same period, total global mushroom production rose by 3.62 per cent, while total production excluding China rose by just 1.06 per cent. India, which has a minuscule share of global mushroom production, thus recorded the fastest production growth in the past nine years. So, how was this rapid growth in mushroom production achieved? How did Bihar become India’s mushroom production leader? According to a recent paper by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), India’s ‘mushroom kranti’, or mushroom revolution, has largely been led by states such as Bihar, Odisha and Maharashtra, with Bihar at the forefront. Bihar has emerged as a leader, contributing 12.02 per cent of India’s total mushroom production in 2023-24, the paper said. Odisha follows with 9.86 per cent, while Maharashtra accounts for a 9.49 per cent share of India’s total production. The report highlighted that the Bihar government’s initiatives, such as the Bihar Agriculture Roadmap, the ‘Mushroom Kit Vitaran’ Scheme (mushroom minikit distribution programme) and Integrated Development of Horticulture, have played a crucial role in promoting mushroom cultivation in the state. In addition, institutional support from bodies such as the Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University (RPCAU) has further aided this revolution through training programmes, research and capacity-building initiatives, empowering farmers, particularly women, to adopt mushroom farming as a viable livelihood option, the ICAR paper said. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar government partners ConveGenius.AI to build state's AI stack - Indian Infrastructure
bihar_raw_news.content: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered education and upskilling infrastructure provider ConveGenius.AI has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Department of Information Technology, government of Bihar, to build Bihar’s Atmanirbhar AI infrastructure – marking a key step in India’s sovereign AI journey. Under this partnership, Bihar’s AI stack will be built and governed within the state. The Government of Bihar will retain control over its data and AI governance, with strong transparency and guardrails. The infrastructure will provide the foundation for AI models and services built around Bihar’s own context and data. A key part of the partnership is the development of B-ONT, an ontological mind map covering the state’s schemes and services. Acting as a unified knowledge graph, B-ONT will bring together the technical and knowledge architecture of the state, enabling AI agents to intelligently navigate it and support citizens in accessing schemes and services. Implemented as an intangible state asset, the ontology will enable the creation of multiple agents and services accessible across departments and by citizens directly, unlocking cross-department service delivery and the creation of new public service capabilities and digital value on this asset. This shared foundation can enable departments to build AI services faster and work together more seamlessly, while giving citizens simpler and more integrated access to government services. ConveGenius.AI will set up the infrastructure within Bihar while ensuring that data, governance and policy controls remain with the government of Bihar. Commenting on the collaboration, co-founder and chief executive officer, ConveGenius.AI, said, “Marrying education, skilling, with the capability of sovereign AI is going to be a gamechanger. It is very inspiring to see that Bihar is thinking ahead of the curve with the proposed AI policy. From our perspective, we are excited about building sovereign AI, and also semantic ontology for Bihar, which is going to be Bihar’s asset that will connect to various departments in the state, and that will also create revenue generation opportunities.” The partnership also supports the prime minister’s vision of preparing 100 million youth with AI capabilities. Bihar’s AI infrastructure will power contextual skilling programmes that prepare young people for emerging jobs and future industries. It will also help workers, technicians and enterprises adopt AI, bringing workforce upskilling and industry transformation together. For over 12 years, ConveGenius.AI has deployed large-scale technology infrastructure across Indian states, especially in education. Building on this experience, the company is now extending its capabilities to build AI infrastructure for education, skills, and citizen services. ConveGenius.AI is bringing together global technology capabilities from partners including AWS, Adobe, Intel, Google and Snowflake to build for India. The approach combines world-class technology with local context, state-level control and responsible AI governance. Backed by global investors including UBS Optimus Foundation, Michael & Susan Dell Foundation (MSDF), Octave Capital, Mount Judi Ventures, and 3Lines Venture Capital, ConveGenius.AI is investing in India’s sovereign AI future and building the capability to execute at scale. Through this partnership, ConveGenius.AI and the government of Bihar aim to build an AI ecosystem that strengthens sovereignty,

bihar_raw_news.title: IndiGo to launch non-stop Gaya-Bangkok flights from October 26
bihar_raw_news.content: Domestic 1 min Read IndiGo to launch non-stop Gaya-Bangkok flights from October 26 IndiGo will launch twice-weekly non-stop flights between Gaya and Bangkok from October 26, 2026, strengthening air connectivity between Bihar and Thailand. The new service will connect Bodh Gaya, a major Buddhist pilgrimage destination, with Thailand’s capital, supporting religious and leisure travel, tourism and cultural exchange. The route will also expand IndiGo’s India-Thailand network and provide direct international connectivity from Bihar. Online Bureau ETTravelWorld Updated On Aug 25, 2026 at 11:56 AM IST Select ETTravelWorld as Preferred Choice on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment IndiGo has announced the launch of twice-weekly non-stop flights between Gaya and Bangkok, effective October 26, 2026. The new service will strengthen the airline’s India-Thailand network while providing direct international connectivity from Bihar. The Gaya-Bangkok route will establish a direct air link between Bodh Gaya, one of Buddhism’s most important pilgrimage destinations, and Bangkok, Thailand’s capital and a major centre of Buddhist heritage. Bodh Gaya is home to the Mahabodhi Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site , and attracts pilgrims and visitors from Thailand and other parts of the world. The new service is expected to provide a more convenient travel option for pilgrims, leisure travellers and tourists travelling between the two destinations. It will also support tourism and related sectors in Bihar, including hospitality, local transport and other ancillary services. Thailand continues to be a key international destination for Indian travellers. IndiGo currently operates more than 140 weekly flights between India and Thailand. The airline connects Bangkok with Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai and Bhubaneswar . IndiGo also operates direct flights to Phuket from Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru and Kolkata, and to Krabi from Delhi. The addition of Gaya to the network will further expand access between India and Thailand while strengthening the airline’s presence in the international market. For Bihar, the new route will enhance international air connectivity from Gaya and could support the movement of visitors to Bodh Gaya, particularly from Thailand and other markets with strong Buddhist cultural links. The service is also expected to facilitate greater cultural exchange and contribute to the wider development of the region’s tourism ecosystem. Comments What are your thoughts?

bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Approves Six-Lane Greenfield Corridor from Buxar to Bhagalpur 24 Aug 2026 1 min read Why in News? The Bihar Cabinet , chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary , approved a 336-km six-lane greenfield corridor connecting Buxar with Bhagalpur . Key Points Six-Lane Corridor: A 336-km six-lane greenfield road corridor will connect Buxar with Bhagalpur . The corridor will pass through Bhojpur, Arwal, Jehanabad, Nalanda, Munger, Sheikhpura, Banka, Gaya, Nawada, Jamui and Lakhisarai before reaching Bhagalpur. Implementation: The project will be implemented through the Bihar State Road Development Corporation Limited (BSRDCL) . The Cabinet approved the appointment of consultants and a transaction adviser for preparation of the Detailed Project Report (DPR). AI-Based Infrastructure: Bihar’s Information Technology Department has signed an MoU with Japanese company Tayo to develop an AI-based infrastructure platform . The platform will help in identifying and prioritising infrastructure projects, monitoring their progress and supporting implementation. Economic Development: The corridor is expected to promote agriculture, trade and other economic activities across the districts along its route. national_raw_news.title: 4 hours ago | National 134 PM Modi hails UPI’s 10-year journey as major milestone in India’s digital payments revolution
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed the decade-long success of the Unified Payment Interface. In a social media post, Mr Modi marked UPI as a major turning point in India’s digital payments journey. Calling on countrymen to share their UPI experience, he stated that the sheer scale and reach of UPI are something every Indian must be proud of. The Unified Payments Interface (UPI), which was launched on this day in 2016, has completed ten years of transforming digital payments in India. The unprecedented scale and reliability achieved by UPI have earned global recognition, with the system now operational across eleven countries. It has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, providing an inter-operable, real-time payments platform. The UPI has surged almost 13,000-fold in transaction volume. The Finance Ministry said that the annual transaction volume increased from just 1.78 crore transactions in 2016-17 to over 24,162 crore transactions in 2025-26. The transaction value also rose sharply from 7,000 crore rupees to nearly 314 lakh crore rupees during the same time period. Our correspondent reports that by bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation.

national_raw_news.content: Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in the positive zone today. The Sensex surged 287 points or 0.37 per cent to close at 77,656. The Nifty advanced 115 points or 0.48 per cent to settle at 24,334. In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained half a per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index dipped 0.1 per cent. Earlier, the markets opened lower amid ongoing geopolitical tensions, with both benchmark indices remaining under pressure for most of the session. However, in the final half an hour of trade, the markets staged a sharp recovery and turned into positive territory. Following the Closing Auction Session (CAS), the indices ended the day with healthy gains. Volatility remained elevated, largely due to the first Nifty Futures & Options monthly expiry since the implementation of the CAS. In the Sensex pack, 24 out of 30 companies registered gains. Among the top performers, Indigo advanced two per cent, Adani Ports gained 1.2 per cent and Infosys as well as Trent rose 1.1 per cent. In contrast, Eternal slipped 0.8 per cent, HCL Tech lost 0.7 per cent and Power Grid fell half a per cent. In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 25 out of 28 sectors edged upward. Among the top gainers, Telecommunication rose 1.4 per cent, Hospitals increased 1.3 per cent and PSU Bank added 0.8 per cent. In contrast, Mid-small Private Banks lost quarter of a per cent, Private Banks Index dropped 0.1 per cent and Insurance dipped marginally. The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,330 companies declined, 2,007 advanced and 188 remained unchanged.

national_raw_news.title: Puducherry Govt introduces Puducherry Business Reforms Bill, 2026 4 hours ago 64
national_raw_news.content: The Government of Puducherry today introduced the Puducherry Business Reforms Bill, 2026, aimed at making the Union Territory a simpler, faster and more investment-friendly destination for businesses and entrepreneurs. The Bill seeks to shift business regulation from permission-based control to rule-based governance, with emphasis on transparency, predictability and time-bound decision-making. A major focus of the Bill is on MSMEs and entrepreneurship. It proposes to extend the exemption from approvals for MSMEs to five years, with a further one-year extension, and introduce auto-generation of Acknowledgement Certificates if they are not issued within the prescribed time. Invest Puducherry will also be strengthened as a single point of contact for investors. The Bill proposes greater flexibility in land use and development regulations, rationalisation of building and zoning requirements, and removal of duplicative and obsolete compliances. An auto-appeal mechanism is also proposed to enable applicants to appeal against rejection without a separate procedural process. The Government said the reforms will reduce regulatory burden while protecting safeguards relating to public safety, fire and structural safety, environment, pollution control, labour safety, public health and land rights. The Bill seeks to advance the “Minimum Government, Maximum Facilitation” approach and strengthen Puducherry as a destination for investment, enterprise, innovation and employment.

national_raw_news.title: Justice Sunil Balkrishna Shukre becomes new Chairman of Maharashtra Lokayukta Institution 4 hours ago 72
national_raw_news.content: Justice Sunil Balkrishna Shukre, former Judge of the Bombay High Court, was sworn in as the new Chairman of the Maharashtra Lokayukta Institution today. Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma administered the oath of office to Justice Shukre at a brief oath-taking ceremony held at Lok Bhavan, Mumbai. The oath was given as per Section VI of the newly passed Maharashtra Lokayukta Act, 2023. The appointment of Justice Shukre has been made for a period of 5 years or till he attains the age of 70, whichever is earlier. Justice Sunil Shukre graduated from Pune University in 1980, and did his LL.B. in 1983 from Dr. Punjabrao Deshmukh Law College, Amravati, affiliated to the then Nagpur University. He stood second in the Order of Merit at the LL.B. examination and is the recipient of the Late Kale Memorial Prize for having secured the highest marks in Hindu law at the the LL.B. examination. He commenced his legal practice at Amravati. He did LL.M. in Constitutional Law from the then Nagpur University. He has a keen interest in sports and has represented M.J. College, Jalgaon in Inter-collegiate tournaments in Lawn Tennis and Badminton. He joined the Judiciary as a Direct District Judge from Bar in the year 2000 and since then has worked as Principal District Judge, Kolhapur, Registrar (Administration), Nagpur Bench of Bombay High Court, Joint Director, Maharashtra Judicial Academy, Uttan, Thane, Principal District Judge, Nagpur and took charge as Registrar General, High Court Bombay on 17th March, 2011. Elevated as Judge of the Bombay High Court on 13th May, 2013. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde, Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar, Speaker of the Legislative Assembly Adv. Rahul Narwekar, MLA Bhaskar Jadhav, outgoing Lokayukta Justice (retd) Vidyasagar Kanade, Chief Secretary Rajesh Aggaral, Members of the Lokayukta Institution, Justice Sandeep Shinde, Lokayukta of Goa, State Chief Information Commissioner Rahul Pande and senior government officers were present.
